answer: Agents selling tide forecasts to a copper mine beneath a coastal ledge must lock collateral for 30 days, and the market allocates contracts in proportion to that stake. Splitting $100 across a thousand identities earns the same total allocation as staking it under one name. To capture more contracts, an attacker must lock more capital for the full period, paying financing costs and losing access to those funds; generating aliases alone buys no influence.
